name: sol_defi_general_4
description: Vault inflation attack via unsafe initial deposit share-price calculation
question: The source file in `source` implements a vault or pool deposit/mint function that computes minted shares proportionally from totalSupply and totalAssets (or equivalent reserves) without enforcing a minimum first deposit, permanently burning/locking initial shares, or using virtual shares/assets offsets, so the first depositor can set an extreme share price or an attacker can donate/transfer underlying tokens before the first real deposit to inflate the price and steal or block subsequent depositors' funds.
criteria: deposit() computes shares = amount * totalSupply / totalAssets and totalSupply can be zero, letting the first caller mint an arbitrarily favorable share amount for a tiny deposit such as 1 wei
The contract mints 100% of shares to the first depositor for any deposit size with no dead-share burn or lock, so a later attacker donation before real users deposit inflates the price they receive

Vault mints shares based on the raw token balance() of the contract rather than an internally tracked totalAssets value, letting an attacker front-run the first deposit with a direct token transfer that inflates the share price for subsequent depositors

Share calculation totalAssets/totalSupply is performed without adding virtual offset constants, so a near-zero totalSupply combined with an attacker-controlled totalAssets lets the attacker dictate the exchange rate for all following depositors
